replication.target_description: Number of women mentioned by respondents of both genders. Target correspondence unresolved unless explicitly stated in notes.

notes: Identity independently checked: title matches Effects of the Generic Masculine and its Alternatives in Germanophone countries; title-page authors begin Hilmar Brohmer and Gabriela Hofer and include the named collaboration, Sczesny, Stahlberg and Athenstaedt. Header Source URL https://osf.io/q56rk/download agrees with the q56rk identifier in the neutral DOI reference. This is an accepted CONFIRMATORY REPORT with final-data Results and Discussion, not a preregistration or abstract-only parse. DOI is not separately printed in the body. Canonical text includes pages 0–44, but Tables 1 and 2 and figures are not text-recovered. No PDF supplied; no rendering possible. Locator pagination differs from this accepted version: p.14 is procedure, p.12 is power planning; substantive final results are pp.21–25. Only unfinished_fields were assessed; original and other unassigned fields are null placeholders. Number of women mentioned by respondents of both genders describes the outcome and inclusion of both sexes but does not identify whether the target is the language-form main effect, a particular contrast, sex main effect or an interaction. The p.12 locator is power planning in this version. Overall successful language-form replication and the replicated sex effect are candidate narrative findings; no row-specific verdict assigned.
